title: Quality gates for Optimize — MVP scope working notes (PM)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- This is a working doc to pin down MVP scope + “what ships vs what is v1”, for the Optimize Quality Guardrails Gating project.
- Optimize changes (batching, caching, quant profiles) can materially change outputs. We need a consistent pre-apply quality check, plus clear exceptions.
- Target outcome for MVP: safe-by-default for hosted API Optimize “one-click apply” and “auto-apply”, without making iteration unbearably slow.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Not redesigning overall model onboarding or eval harness fundamentals.
- Not delivering full automation for Private / on-prem (we’ll define workflow, docs, and data model; automation later).
- Not guaranteeing zero quality change. Goal is to prevent silent regressions and make risk visible + auditable.

Audience
- Optimize product + engineering, Applied ML/Evals, Rollouts/Console, SRE.
- This doc is specifically for internal alignment; wording below includes draft customer messaging snippets.


MVP definition (what must be true to call this “done”)
1) Any Optimize-generated config recommendation that will touch production traffic must have a Gate Run.
   - Gate Run is an offline eval comparison (baseline vs proposed config) with pass/fail outcome.
   - Console shows gate status + top reasons when failing.
2) Apply boundary enforcement: cannot apply config if gate failed or missing.
   - Enforcement must exist at Optimize API level (not only UI).
   - Defense-in-depth: rollout controller must block canary promotion if gate later becomes invalid / missing.
3) Tiered gates to keep UX fast:
   - Fast smoke gates for batching + caching diffs (quick feedback).
   - Full gates required for quantization profile changes (higher risk).
4) Clear override workflow:
   - Time-bound override with required justification.
   - Audit trail: who approved, why, what evidence, expiration.
5) Observability + supportability:
   - Metrics on pass/fail, flake rate, latency, timeouts; basic dashboards.
   - Runbook link from alerts / console.


Supported config change types (MVP)
In-scope
- Batching policy updates (e.g., max batch size, continuous batching policy changes).
- Prefix/KV caching settings (enable/disable, thresholds, cache sizing policies exposed to Optimize).
- Quantization profile changes (per model family + GPU SKU).

Out-of-scope (MVP) — explicitly not blocking in code? (needs decision)
- Model version change / model swap (handled by existing model rollout processes; but we may want to reuse the gate mechanism later).
- Prompt templates changes (customer-level prompt changes, not platform changes).
- Decoder behavior changes (temperature, top_p) — these are app-level parameters; Optimize may recommend defaults but we’re not gating those yet.

Note: “Out-of-scope” still needs logging if applied via other mechanisms.


Gate tiers: smoke vs full (draft)
Smoke gate (MVP)
- Purpose: catch obvious regressions quickly and avoid blocking engineers for hours.
- Applies to: batching + caching diffs by default.
- Prompt subset: small, representative (owned by Jonas/Selene). Should include:
  - short factual Q/A
  - instruction following with strict formatting
  - a few long-context prompts if caching is involved
- Runtime target: 10–20 minutes (p95), bounded cost.
- Pass/fail: coarse thresholds; designed to be stable.
- Retry: allow 1 rerun if flake score is high (from eval harness), otherwise fail.

Full gate (MVP)
- Purpose: higher confidence for higher-risk changes.
- Applies to: quant profile diffs always; optionally for “risky” caching/batching combos.
- Prompt set: broader coverage; require min sample size and confidence handling.
- Runtime target: 60–120 minutes (p95) is acceptable for “apply to prod” but must not break rollout pipelines.
- Pass/fail: stricter + more metrics (see below).

Open decision (still not fully resolved): do we require full gate after smoke gate for caching/batching before *full rollout*, even if canary passes?
- Option A (simpler): Smoke gate required for apply; online canary signals are the second gate.
- Option B (safer): Smoke gate for apply to canary; full gate required before promote.
- Current leaning (2026-02-12): Option A for MVP, with policy hooks to turn on Option B per route/tier later (see pr-19588 for policy config).


Quality metrics for gates (MVP summary)
Pulled from Applied ML discussions; exact thresholds live in Confluence v1 doc.
- Primary: task success rate / rubric score (depending on prompt set) + structured output validity where applicable.
- Secondary: “format adherence” and safety policy checks (don’t regress on refusal patterns).
- Guardrails: minimum sample size, confidence interval / variance modeling (Sana). If variance too high -> classify as “inconclusive” and require rerun or full gate.

We need one “human readable” failure reason in Console:
- e.g., “Structured output validity dropped by 2.3% (threshold: 0.5%)”
- e.g., “Rubric score delta -0.12 exceeded threshold -0.05 (p<0.05)”

Open question: how do we avoid bikeshedding over metric choice per prompt set?
- Proposal: metrics are owned by Evals team; Optimize product only chooses which *tier* is required per change type, plus what the default policy is.


Gating policy by account tier / route (MVP)
- Default policy (hosted API):
  - Self-serve routes: smoke gate for batching/caching; full gate for quant.
  - Enterprise routes (SLA / regulated): full gate for quant; smoke gate + stricter online canary requirements for batching/caching.
- Per-route overrides allowed (for internal and early design partners), but must be visible in Console + audit log.

Open question: do we allow “auto-apply” for self-serve at MVP?
- Yes, but only when gate passes + route policy allows.
- For enterprise, auto-apply likely disabled by default until we have more evidence.


State machine notes (MVP)
(Keep simple; details in system design)
- pending -> running -> passed | failed | inconclusive
- overridden is a separate terminal status, but should retain the underlying failed/inconclusive reason.
- cancelled should be possible when config changes or user aborts.

Important product behavior:
- Gate results are tied to a specific config diff + baseline + model family + hardware sku.
- Re-using an old gate run should be disallowed if baseline changed (model version, prompt set version, harness version) — unless policy explicitly allows.


Baseline selection (quant) — what we decided so far
- Baseline for quant profile gating must be per model family + GPU SKU (runtime correctness issues can be SKU-specific).
- Baseline is “current production profile” for that route/model/SKU, not a generic default.
- If the route is new / no baseline exists: choose “Redwood recommended default” and mark gate as “lower confidence” until online signals confirm.

Edge case: route has mixed SKUs (autoscaling across pools)
- MVP: choose baseline per SKU; gate must pass on all SKUs used by that route OR restrict rollout to the SKUs tested.
- This needs buy-in from Runtime/SRE; may impact rollout controller logic.


Offline vs online (canary) signals — coupling decisions
- Offline gates are mandatory before apply (MVP).
- Online canary signals are mandatory before promotion to 100% for changes that affect >X% of production traffic (X TBD).
- If online signals show regression, auto-rollback hooks must trigger and the gate should be flagged as “passed offline but failed online” (important for learning + prompt set updates).

Open question: define minimum online canary window
- Proposal: 30–60 minutes minimum, depending on traffic volume.
- Enterprise low-traffic routes: may need longer windows or synthetic traffic (tbd).


Override policy (MVP product shape)
- Overrides allowed but intentionally frictionful.
- Must specify:
  - reason category (e.g., “false positive / flaky eval”, “business critical”, “known acceptable behavior change”)
  - justification text
  - expiration (max 7 days for MVP; discuss)
  - owner (person accountable)
- Approvers:
  - MVP: Optimize oncall + PM + Evals lead (one of) depending on reason category.
  - Need RBAC role in Console (“quality_gate_override_approver”).

Explicitly *not* allowed:
- Permanent overrides.
- Overrides without audit log.


Edge cases / scary cases list (needs explicit handling or at least known limitations)
1) Eval harness timeouts or regional GPU scarcity
- Should not block forever; show “inconclusive: timeout” and allow rerun.
- Product decision: do we allow override if timeouts happen repeatedly? Probably yes with SRE signoff.

2) Flaky prompt sets
- Need quarantine workflow (admin tooling). If a suite is quarantined:
  - Gate should either skip that suite with prominent warning OR fail closed.
  - MVP leaning: fail closed for enterprise policies, warn-and-continue for self-serve (policy controlled).

3) Caching change that only impacts long-context
- Smoke prompt set must include long-context cases, otherwise we’ll miss this.
- We should flag caching changes as “risk: long context” and require expanded coverage when avg context length for the route > threshold.

4) Batching changes that alter tail latency and indirectly quality (timeouts / truncation)
- Offline gate might not capture. Need online SLO signals.

5) “Equivalent” config diffs
- Some runtime knobs might be semantically equivalent (Noah/Sofia mentioned). If we can canonicalize diffs, we can reuse gate results. Risky; probably v1.

6) Customer uses custom stop sequences / structured output
- Gate prompt sets might not match. We should at minimum include a structured-output validity metric for any route that has schema enforcement enabled.

7) Multi-model routing / fallback policies
- If route can fallback to another model, offline gate might run on one model but production might shift.
- MVP: gate must run against the primary model; if fallback happens during canary, canary results are noisy.
- Need a “gate is only valid when primary model share >= Y%” constraint (maybe later).


MVP scope decisions (current as of 2026-02-12)
- Must-have:
  - Gate enforcement at apply boundary (API)
  - Smoke gate for batching/caching
  - Full gate for quant
  - Override flow with expiration + audit
  - Console surface for pass/fail + artifact links
  - Rollout controller blocks promotion on missing/failed gate
  - Basic dashboards + runbook

- Nice-to-have if it lands “for free” during implementation:
  - Per-route policy config
  - “Inconclusive” classification with automatic rerun
  - Simple flaky-suite detection

- Not MVP:
  - Sophisticated reuse of prior gate runs across similar diffs
  - Automated Private/on-prem enforcement
  - Customer-configurable thresholds (we own thresholds centrally)


Draft customer messaging (internal draft — not final copy)
Positioning sentence
- “Optimize now includes Quality Gates: before cost-saving changes can be applied to production traffic, we automatically run evaluations to ensure output quality remains within your configured tolerance.”

What happens when a gate fails
- “If a proposed optimization is predicted to degrade quality beyond the allowed threshold, Redwood blocks the change from being applied and surfaces the specific metrics and evaluation artifacts so you can review and decide next steps.”

Fast vs full gate explanation
- “We use a tiered approach: a fast evaluation for most batching/caching changes, and a more comprehensive evaluation for higher-risk changes like quantization profile updates.”

Override framing (careful wording)
- “In exceptional cases, authorized admins can apply a time-bound override with a documented rationale. All overrides are logged for audit purposes.”

FAQ snippet: ‘Will this slow down my ability to save costs?’
- “Most recommendations complete a fast gate within minutes. Higher-risk changes may take longer to validate. You can still review results and schedule application windows, and we provide clear visibility into gate runtime and status.”

FAQ snippet: ‘Is this required?’
- “Quality Gates are required for Optimize recommendations that affect production traffic, as part of Redwood’s safe-by-default production controls.”


Launch notes (limited beta)
- Beta cohorts: internal routes + select customers who already asked for stricter controls.
- Go/no-go for limited rollout:
  - Smoke gate p95 runtime within target
  - Flake rate below threshold (tbd)
  - <1% of gate runs stuck in running >2 hours
  - No high-sev incident attributable to gating deadlocks / blocking deploys


Open questions (please comment inline / ping Aditya)
1) Do we require full gate before 100% promotion for batching/caching? (see earlier)
2) What’s the default behavior for “inconclusive”?
   - fail closed vs allow canary with warning
3) What is the max override duration for MVP (7 days? 72 hours?)
4) Should “auto-apply” be disabled by default for enterprise routes until we have 30 days of data?
5) How do we represent gate validity if baseline changes? (invalidate vs soft warning)
6) How do we handle EU region timeouts (support ticket trend suggests this will happen)? Need SRE plan.


Notes / breadcrumbs from recent discussions
- Slack #product (MVP scope): agreement that quant needs stricter gating; debate on requiring full gate for caching.
- Slack #architecture: enforcement should be defense-in-depth (Optimize API + rollout controller).
- Applied ML: metric thresholds must account for variance; avoid overreacting to tiny deltas.
- Runtime: quant+long-context is a known risk corner; ensure prompt sets cover.


Next steps
- Aditya + Talia: finalize MVP scope bullets for PRD + launch plan (PM-481)
- Jonas/Selene/Sana: confirm metric set + initial thresholds + flake handling
- Paula: confirm rollout coupling behavior (halt vs rollback)
- Dylan/Chloe: confirm Console UX for failure reasons + override request path
- Sean/Allison: confirm alerting strategy that won’t page on flake storms
